title: Component manifest (nanosoc-component.yaml at a repo's root)
description: Hand-written by each repo. The tool reads dependencies, variants and tests from it instead of guessing. Phase 3 (C11); validated by T0 gate t0.manifest.valid from v1 on, which records SKIP while no repo carries one. Eligibility (silicon, frozen, auto-merge) is NOT here: it lives in the registry, where the target repo cannot change it. C1, C6, C7, C11, D1, D6, E1, E3, I2.

id.description: C11: equals the registry catalogue id.

class.description: C11: equals the catalogue class (loader checks).

version.description: C1, C11. On a release commit it equals the tag, unless the tag is grandfathered (C10).

canonical.description: C11: canonical clone URL. HTTPS only, so a stranger can clone it (D2).

provides.description: C11: named interfaces this repo offers, each with an integer interface version.

requires.description: C11, E1: direct submodule dependencies with the version range this repo accepts. `path` is the gitlink path.

reexports.description: C6: component ids this repo passes through to its users. Its change class is at least theirs.

variants.description: C7: per build variant, the command that prints the resolved file list. The build-affecting flag is computed from diffs of these lists.

generated.description: DEC10 b, G7: where generated RTL is written and whether it is committed. build_soc/ stays gitignored, so releases archive it.

tests.description: C11, D1: test entry point per tier. Exit code 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 NOT-RUN. `control` is the negative control for the same tier (D6): it must exit 1.

workarounds.description: E3 (Phase 4): local workaround files, and the upstream commit whose arrival retires each one. A bump that retires one goes to a person.

fork_contract.description: I2 (Phase 5, example projects): the upstream and the paths users own.
